source.title: Enhancing Sharpness-Aware Optimization Through Variance Suppression

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether SAM’s adversarial sharpness estimate relates to generalization and argues its benefit is conditional: a minibatch-specific adversary can be friendly, and its stated m-sharpness relation is not universal. It also reports its own SAM/VaSSO generalization and sharpness measurements.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own reported classification and translation performance comparisons, its explicit perturbation-variance results, and its Hessian-spectrum measurements. Theoretical convergence and variance bounds are not empirical generalization-gap results. Cited prior work is not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses the sharpness–generalization premise to develop VaSSO and reports optimizer performance and Hessian curvature. It does not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance against measured generalization gaps. Its arguments about minibatch adversaries and m-sharpness concern different constructs, and none of V1–V8 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that VaSSO provably stabilizes adversary construction and empirically improves performance over SAM across their tested vision and translation tasks, with substantial robustness gains under high label noise. This is not a demonstration of V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–gap correlation.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes VaSSO, an exponentially averaged stochastic linearization for SAM, then compares it with SAM and other SAM-family optimizers. Its reported tasks use standard image or translation datasets and data augmentation; it does not reproduce the original claim's random-label or train-test-gap experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varied with VaSSO theta; the paper reports theta=0.4 best for ResNet-18 and WRN-28-10 on CIFAR10, theta=0.9 best in other CIFAR10 settings, and theta=0.2 best among tested VaSSO settings under each label-noise level. On IWSLT-14, BLEU varied with theta. The m-SAM result also varied by dataset/task.

fits_no_version.finding: VaSSO improves reported test accuracy over SAM across the tested image classifiers and improves translation BLEU, with results depending on theta.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suppressing variance in SAM's adversary construction can improve held-out performance over SAM.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet-18 Hessian summaries decrease from SGD to SAM to VaSSO: largest eigenvalues are 82.52, 26.40 and 23.32; eigenvalue ratios are 16.63, 2.12 and 1.86.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this augmented CIFAR10 experiment, SAM and VaSSO produce lower Hessian curvature summaries alongside higher test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Using an independent minibatch to construct the adversary nearly erases SAM's accuracy advantage; adding gradient noise also degrades performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM's held-out performance depends on how its stochastic adversarial perturbation is constructed.

fits_no_version.finding: Transformer test BLEU decreases as the adversary batch shrinks on IWSLT-14 despite tuning rho.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Smaller adversary batches do not universally improve SAM's held-out performance.

fits_no_version.finding: At 75% label noise, VaSSO with theta=0.2 reaches 85.02% accuracy versus SAM's 75.36%; at 25% noise, theta=0.9 is slightly below SAM and the other differences are small.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: VaSSO's advantage over SAM under label noise depends on noise level and theta, with the largest gains at high noise and smaller tested theta.

record.problems: The paper reports only averaged results over 2 independent runs for ImageNet ResNet-50. Several conclusions use test-accuracy comparisons rather than direct train-test gaps. Figure 1 numeric values are not provided in text. Table 5 uses an approximate Hessian spectrum and gives no uncertainty. The label-noise excerpt does not identify the model architecture.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same recipe, including chance-level held-out performance for random labels.
Test-error behavior when width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under controlled tuning conditions; adaptive SAM variants are not this comparison.
Training batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance; changing only the adversary batch does not test this.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, underfitting, and joint removal with weight decay.

Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus measured generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, including rankings against norm and margin measures. Hessian summaries and m-sharpness arguments do not establish these results.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No supplied version receives a verdict. The m-sharpness counterexample and partition-dependence argument in Appendix B address a different sharpness formulation. Figure 1(c) also includes m=b/4 and m=b/8, omitted from the record, but these do not bear on a supplied version. Some Figure 1(a–b) numeric annotations survive in the supplied text, so the record's blanket statement that their numbers are unavailable is too strong.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization versus natural-label generalization; no random-label fitting or held-out chance comparison is reported.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Optimizer comparisons are within SAM-family setups; the paper does not test adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the version’s tuning conditions.

It measures Hessian eigenvalue summaries in one ResNet-18 setting, not magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or a ranking against norm- and margin-based measures; no data-augmentation-free setting is tested.
No example removal or retraining experiment.

relation.reason: The study discusses sharpness and generalization and uses that premise to develop VaSSO, but its experiments do not measure the outcomes specified by V1–V8. Hessian eigenvalues are not V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or a measured training–test gap.

tranche.reason: The paper develops VaSSO using sharpness and generalization arguments, then reports its optimizer performance and curvature measures. It does not test any supplied claim version.

source_check.notes: The recovered source is arXiv:2309.15639v3, by Bingcong Li and Georgios B. Giannakis. Figure 1(b)'s legend identifies variance settings 10^-6, 10^-4, and 10^-2; its plotted test accuracies are normalized to SGD and remain figure-only here. No other omitted result bearing on V1–V8 was found.
